messages:
alex_support: Customer ACME reporting repeated 503s and large tail latency on hosted /v1/generate since ~10:12 UTC. Multiple API retries, several customers impacted.
jen_sre: seeing the same in SLO dashboards — spike in upstream 5xx from infer-runner pool, many pods restarting.
ops-bot: note: deploy event 4319994300 rolled quant-optimizer v4 to canary group at 10:08 UTC.
lee_runtime: that rollout includes a kernel selection change and a quant swap path tweak. possible mem regression.
alex_support: pasted truncated logs from ACME: `POST /v1/generate 503 0.003s` repeating, clients see 500/503 intermittently.
jen_sre: kubectl logs show `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'` then `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` for infer-runner in affected pods.
lee_runtime: nvidia-smi snapshots captured during the window show GPU memory saturating to 100% then process killed.
sam_devex: quick config check — canary group had `batch_size` bumped to 64 yesterday in the canary policy.
marc_oncall: temporarily rerouting canary traffic to fallback-small model pool and enabling extra headroom. applying now. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: routing change applied to 3 canary nodes (policy=fallback-small).
jen_sre: error rate dropped after reroute but a few pods still OOM/restart under stress tests. need root cause.
lee_runtime: short repro command that reproduces locally in ~90s: `scripts/loadtest/runner_qps.sh --qps 120 --ctx 4096 --model quant-v4 --batch 64` — shows OOM followed by segfault.
alex_support: ACME asked for ETA. can we provide mitigation + timeline?
jen_sre: immediate mitigation = keep canary on fallback routing, reduce batch_size to 16 for affected model, disable kv_prefetch for canary, and rollback quant-optimizer v4 from canary.
lee_runtime: agreed. also need collection steps for a core dump and previous logs if it happens again.
jen_sre: commands to run on affected node (short):
```
kubectl get pods -n hosted -o wide | grep infer-runner
kubectl describe pod <pod>
kubectl logs <pod> --container=infer-runner --previous
journalctl -u docker -o short-precise | tail -n200
dmesg | tail -n100
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv -l 1
```
lee_runtime: looking at kernel logs we saw `Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (infer-runner)` and an oom_reaper entry right before segfault. memory alloc path in quant swap likely unbounded under high ctx + batch.
sam_devex: recommend temporary policy changes: batch cap 16, disable kv_prefetch, enable fallback routing for latency > 500ms, and add short-term autoscale headroom.
alex_support: I've updated the ACME ticket with the mitigation plan and will follow up in 30m.
marc_oncall: initiating rollback of quant-optimizer v4 on canary nodes now.
deploy-bot: rollback triggered: quant-optimizer v3 -> canary group.
ops-bot: alert posted to #eng-runtime: high-oom-rate detected on infer-runner canary after 10:08 deploy.
lee_runtime: after rollback local repro shows memory footprint reduced and no segfault within same load window. planning hotfix: add allocation bounds and guard in quant-swap code path + max-batch cap at runtime.
jen_sre: ticketing: collecting previous pod logs (kubectl logs --previous), core artifacts if produced, and node dmesg for postmortem.
lee_runtime: if it recurs please set `echo /tmp/core.%e.%p > /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` and upload core + infer-runner binary to S3 bucket `s3://redwood-debug/4319994321/`. also gdb attach instructions saved to the incident runbook.
sam_devex: enabling temporary autoscale headroom and adding a routing rule to send >95th percentile latency traffic to dedicated pool.
alex_support: ACME confirms improved behavior, some residual retries but no widespread 503s. will keep them posted.
lee_runtime: next steps: create patch with allocation checks, add unit/regression test for quant swap, and schedule a controlled rollout once we validate on load.
jen_sre: will own postmortem with timeline and impact metrics after 24h of stability.
alex_support: thanks all — keeping ticket open until 2h stable then will update customer and close. :thumbsup:
